results.fact: Where/at what elevation the spur leaves the PCT
results.evidence: Two sources put the spur's start at the PCT's crest (~7,600-7,650 ft, its Washington high point), supporting pitch_detail and crowds. But WTA describes a lower unmarked split (right through boulders to Old Snowy, left toward Elk Pass) and another description puts a junction at 7,190 ft; the waypoint[4] pin itself sits at ~7,075 ft on the USGS 1 m DEM and its note (pack stash) matches the upper point. The row appears to conflate two junctions; waypoint elev not changed without resolving which point the pin represents.

results.fact: Line of the summit scramble (south-ridge saddle vs Old Snowy-Ives col)
results.evidence: Neither version is confirmed. Oregon Hikers says follow the PCT to its ~7,650 ft crest, then follow the ridge SOUTH on a small trail to the summit; a 2017 trip report calls the final stretch a scramble up Old Snowy's NORTH ridge. That contradicts both the 'south-ridge saddle' (approach, climbing_route, route name) and the itinerary's Old Snowy-Ives col (Ives lies to the south-southeast). Needs owner review of the whole route geometry rather than a one-field patch.

The two sources found put the standard summit path on the ridge NORTH of the summit (walked southward from the PCT crest; the PCT runs on the peak's west slopes), which supports aspect NW / face 'Northwest shoulder' and contradicts the route name 'South Ridge' and beta's 'south side'. The name cannot be changed here and the south-ridge claim runs through approach, climbing_route and approach_variants, so this is flagged rather than patched.

results.fact: Parking pass at Snowgrass Flats trailhead
results.correct_value: A $5/day or $30/year Northwest Forest Pass (or valid Recreation Pass) is required at the Snowgrass trailhead as well as Berry Patch
results.evidence: The Forest Service's Snowgrass Trailhead page lists it as a fee site: $5 per vehicle per day, $30 annual, payable by cash, check, Scan & Pay or a Recreation Pass. A 2025 Gifford Pinchot release says Snowgrass Trailhead became a new $5/day Northwest Forest Pass site once the new vault toilet was installed (the row notes the vault toilet). An older hike page also lists 'NW Forest Pass Required'. The 'not required' claims are older and pre-date the change.
